stories.label: At least 18 killed in Houthi attack on military camp in Yemen's Shabwa
stories.summary: Three Houthi ballistic missiles hit the al-Alam camp in Shabwa during a training exercise, killing at least 18 government soldiers. Lead with the toll and the target: a southern governorate far from the Saudi-backed west-coast offensive, which shows the Houthis can reach deep behind the front as the Saudi–Yemen war widens (Saudi helicopter crash near Najran, Egypt's delayed troop vote). Name who fired, who died and where; don't flatten it into 'clashes'.

stories.label: Lavrov visits Iran as Russia explores role in US-Tehran talks
stories.summary: Lavrov is in Tehran after GCC states asked Moscow to help halt Iranian attacks and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The shift to lead with: Gulf monarchies allied to Washington are turning to Russia as a broker in a US–Iran war. Explain what Moscow gains (leverage over the US on Ukraine, oil revenue from high Brent) and how this differs from Iran's earlier proposal to reopen Hormuz through Baghdad. Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is the series to name.

stories.label: Saudi Arabia Executes 2 Bangladeshis Over 'Indecent Acts,' and Other Mideast News
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia executed two Bangladeshi workers in Mecca for 'indecent acts' without telling Dhaka beforehand, and Bangladesh is now asking why. Lead with the missing notice: consular notification is a basic duty under the Vienna Convention, and migrant workers from South Asia make up a large share of the people Saudi Arabia executes. Name the Saudi authorities who carried it out and the Bangladeshi ministry asking for answers.

stories.label: SHC dismisses state appeal against Mahrang's 2025 acquittal in sedition case
stories.summary: The Sindh High Court threw out the provincial government's appeal against Baloch rights leader Mahrang Baloch's acquittal on terrorism and sedition charges, calling it non-maintainable. Lead with the court rebuffing the state: Pakistan has used terrorism and sedition laws against the Baloch Yakjehti Committee's peaceful protests over enforced disappearances. Set it beside the governor's rule and emergency the Centre imposed on Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on 11 October, which shows how far Islamabad is now governing by emergency powers.

stories.label: VW Plans to Freeze Salaries Through 2030
stories.summary: IG Metall says Volkswagen wants to freeze pay for more than 660,000 employees worldwide until 2030 as union talks begin. Lead with the scale and the length: four years of frozen pay with inflation running, so a real pay cut. Explain the mechanism: Chinese EV competition and the cost of restructuring are being passed to workers rather than shareholders. Give the union's response and what happens next in the talks.

stories.label: Canada's annual inflation rate rose to 3.1% in September
stories.summary: Canada's inflation rose to 3.1% in September, above the Bank of Canada's 1-3% band for the first time in three months, pushed up by gasoline and diesel. Lead with the cause: the Gulf war is keeping Brent crude near $110, and this is that war reaching household prices in a G7 economy far from the fighting. Core measures eased (Bloomberg), so give the Bank of Canada's dilemma ahead of its next rate decision. The series to name is Brent crude.

stories.label: PBOC plans bond liquidity backstop, pilots onshore yuan trade for foreign banks
stories.summary: China's central bank will set up a liquidity facility for non-bank financial institutions to stop mass fund redemptions turning into systemic bond-market stress, and will let foreign banks trade the yuan onshore in a pilot. Lead with the backstop: the PBOC is acting as lender of last resort to funds, not just banks, which shows where Beijing sees the risk. Then explain the opening to foreign banks as part of making the yuan more international. This is not the Q3 GDP story already covered. The series to name is the yuan.

stories.label: US Moves to Bar DeepSeek From Federal Agencies and Contracts
stories.summary: The Trump administration ordered civilian federal agencies to remove DeepSeek products and services and barred them from contracts. Lead with the reason given against the reason that matters: officials cite security, but DeepSeek's cheap open-weight models threaten Silicon Valley's pricing, and this is industrial policy as much as security policy. Explain how far the ban reaches (contractors, open weights run on US servers). WARNING to writer: only the Bloomberg link is about DeepSeek. The Economic Times and The Hill links in sources are about Musk's SpaceX share pledge, so do not use them.

stories.label: How a Massive Chinese Crime Ring Hacked Staples to Steal Millions
stories.summary: An organised crime ring broke into Staples' systems, issued itself millions of dollars in gift cards and spent them across the US. Lead with the mechanism: gift cards are a weak point in retail security because they can be issued in bulk and turned into goods almost at once. Explain how the intrusion worked, how it was found, and what it shows about retailers' internal controls. Attribute 'Chinese' to the investigators 404 Media cites.

stories.label: European telecoms groups join forces to challenge Elon Musk's Starlink
stories.summary: Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica and Vodafone are exploring a joint bid for spectrum to offer satellite-to-phone service against Starlink. Lead with the motive: after Starlink became leverage in Ukraine (Bessent's warning to Zelenskyy), Europe's biggest carriers see dependence on one American billionaire's network as a sovereignty risk. Explain direct-to-device spectrum and why carriers are racing for it, and compare IRIS², the EU's own satellite programme.

stories.label: Jev刚火，国产29B开源模型来踢馆了！不光会判断，还能直接填参数
stories.summary: China Telecom's AI lab open-sourced Xing4.0-29B-Intent, a model built only for turning spoken instructions into structured commands for agents. It came with 2.75 million training examples drawn from 61 datasets in 52 languages, under Apache 2.0. Lead with the split this points to: small specialist models do the high-volume intent parsing in under 150ms, and large models are left for reasoning. That is a cost argument for running agents on phones and in cars. Give the benchmark claims (zero-shot F1 70.27, ahead of GPT-4.1) as the lab's own figures. The reason it matters: a Chinese state-owned telecom is releasing the training data as well as the weights.

stories.label: Ancient Hox code reveals the developmental roots of vertebrate hind fins and limbs
stories.summary: Researchers traced how the Hox gene system that builds paired fins, and later our arms and legs, was assembled during evolution, focusing on the roots of hind fins and limbs. Lead with what the reader would miss: the genetic toolkit for legs existed in fish ancestors before limbs did, and was repurposed rather than invented. Name the journal, the species studied and the specific finding about the origin of pelvic fins.

stories.label: 1.4 million Palestinians still acutely food insecure in Gaza
stories.summary: The WFP says funding shortages forced it to cut Gaza food aid by about a third, leaving half a million people without support as winter comes, while 1.4 million remain acutely food insecure. Lead with the half-million cut off and name who holds the levers: the donors whose money dried up and the Israeli controls on what enters. The mechanism is a famine-adjacent population whose survival rests on a voluntary funding stream.

stories.label: Putin Approves Major Government Cabinet Reshuffle
stories.summary: Weeks after United Russia won its largest-ever Duma majority, Putin replaced nearly half of Mishustin's deputies, with Finance Minister Anton Siluanov among four officials raised to deputy prime minister. Lead with the scale of the turnover, and explain who now runs the war economy's purse strings and what the moves signal about succession and wartime budget priorities.

stories.label: Helen Haines is in a critical condition after an alleged attack. Here's what we know so far
stories.summary: Independent MP Helen Haines is critically injured after an alleged vehicle attack outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, and the driver is arrested. Stick to what is confirmed. The structural point is the exposure of lawmakers at their local offices, after a run of attacks on legislators in other democracies.

stories.label: Indonesian Stock Exchange Plunges After Fresh MSCI Downgrade Threat
stories.summary: MSCI proposed demoting Indonesia from emerging-market to standalone status, citing promised market reforms that never came, and Jakarta's index plunged. The mechanism is that index demotion forces passive funds to sell, so foreign capital leaves the largest Muslim-majority economy. Name the rupiah and who pays: Indonesian savers and firms raising capital.

stories.label: Minister Bayraktar was asked directly: When will we be freed from foreign dependence in energy?
stories.summary: Turkey sent off the Osman Gazi floating production platform, which will double output from the Black Sea Sakarya gas field. Lead with the doubling. The figure to land is what share of Turkey's gas imports, mostly from Russia and Iran, that covers, at a time when Gulf war prices are high. Treat the energy minister's independence claims as claims, and give the actual import share.

stories.label: Hong Kong Freezes Billions in Probe of Artificial IPO Demand
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission halted trading in three listed companies and froze over HK$4.6 billion while it investigates whether IPO placings were propped up with recycled funds. Lead with the freeze. The mechanism is faked subscription demand, which misleads every later buyer, and it puts the integrity of Hong Kong's IPO revival on trial.

stories.label: 约20%的Anthropic股份，将用于公益！
stories.summary: Anthropic will put 5% of its shares into a Public Benefit Fund aimed at AI-driven job losses, with 2% more each time its valuation rises 50%. With founder and employee pledges, that brings about 20% of the company to public purposes. The fund is an LLC, not a charity, so it can pay people directly, and it is barred from lobbying. Musk answered by promising a SpaceX share to every American child. The question is whether equity in an AI lab can compensate the workers it displaces.

stories.label: 华人00后做“本地Muse”，被硅谷AI圈疯抢，a16z和Anthropic都投了
stories.summary: Conway Research's Underdog is a personal AI agent that runs entirely on the user's device, offline, on a fine-tuned Qwen 27B model, with a custom inference engine it says is 4.5x faster than Apple's MLX. Investors include a16z and Anthropic's fund. The contrast to draw is with Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dot, which run each user's agent on a cloud VM and see their data: here a Chinese open-weight model is the base of a privacy-first US product.

stories.label: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to "play.
stories.summary: Researchers left solo AI agents on a virtual island for 30 hours with no task, and the agents invented games such as basketball and 'the floor is lava'. Lead with what agents do when nobody directs them. That matters as autonomous agents spread, because their undirected behaviour is what runs in the background. Keep the 'is it really play' question sceptical.

stories.label: El Niño is dramatically increasing sea levels - how bad could it get? | New Scientist
stories.summary: The record El Niño has already raised sea levels in parts of the eastern Pacific by 40 cm and is still strengthening, so coastal flooding is possible from Alaska to Chile. Lead with the 40 cm. Explain the mechanism (warm water expanding and piling eastward as the trade winds weaken) and who is exposed: Peruvian and Ecuadorian coastal cities and fisheries.

stories.label: Putin wants to meet Trump and Xi to discuss a deal on Ukraine - WSJ
stories.summary: Putin has proposed a three-way summit next month with Trump and Xi to settle the Ukraine war on terms that favour Moscow, the Wall Street Journal reports — a format that would put Beijing at the table and leave Kyiv and Europe outside it. Lead with who is in the room and who is not; note the same weekend Trump accused Zelenskyy of never wanting the war to end, after Ukraine's drone strikes on Russian refineries. Attribute the summit claim to the WSJ's sources and TASS's account to Russian state media. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: Lula and Bolsonaro trade barbs in fiery Brazil run-off debate
stories.summary: A week before the 25 October run-off, Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro — standing in for his convicted father's movement — met in their first debate of a tight race. Lead with what the race is now about beyond the insults: the policy lines each drew on the economy and the courts, and what the polls show. Latin America is under its dateline target; this is the region's biggest election. Dateline São Paulo.

stories.label: Companies exploiting welfare system by using residents as 'cash cows,' BBC finds
stories.summary: A BBC Panorama investigation finds private property firms recruiting vulnerable people through social media into 'supported housing', collecting their taxpayer-funded housing benefit and failing to give the support they are paid for. Lead with the mechanism — the exempt-accommodation loophole that lets landlords claim higher rates with little oversight — and name the companies and the Department for Work and Pensions' response. Accountability story: who profits, who is housed badly. Dateline Birmingham if the investigation centres there, otherwise London.

stories.label: Iran urges US to accept proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: New development since yesterday's coverage of Iran's proposal: Araghchi, in Baghdad, gave its terms — Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz within six days and talks with the US would resume on the seventh if Washington accepts its conditions. Hours later the IRGC Navy said another tanker hit a mine in the southern strait and caught fire (Iranian state media Mehr; attribute). Lead with the six-day timetable against the mine strike, then name the series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude. Dateline Baghdad.

stories.label: Growers end losers in 'flawed' wheat market reform
stories.summary: Pakistan's third wheat season since it scrapped the official support price and suspended large-scale state procurement in April 2025, under IMF pressure, may be its most uncertain: the promised market-based system left growers selling below cost while traders and millers set prices. Lead with what farmers now get per maund against input costs, and who captured the margin; name the series, wheat. Dateline Lahore.

stories.label: Bitcoin jumps to $82,500, stocks rise as China GDP beats estimates
stories.summary: The story is China, not bitcoin: the economy grew 4.5% year on year in the third quarter, and retail sales beat expectations, a sign of domestic demand holding up while a Gulf war pushes oil near $110. Lead with the GDP figure and what drove it (consumption versus exports and investment), then what it means for the yuan and for Asian markets that rallied on it. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: SEC tokenized stock framework faces issuer pushback as Broadcom, Verizon, Nasdaq object listing
stories.summary: Under the SEC's temporary framework, crypto venues such as OKX can list blockchain tokens of public companies' shares — and Broadcom, Verizon and Nasdaq have objected to having their stock tokenized without their consent. Lead with the consent question: who controls a company's shares once a token of them trades on another venue, and what the issuers fear (shareholder records, voting, liability). Explain the framework's mechanism plainly. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: 220亿机器人明星项目，打五折卖不出去
stories.summary: Secondary shares in a Chinese robotics star valued at 22 billion yuan, fought over last year, now cannot find buyers even at half price. Lead with the discount and the company, then the mechanism: what has cooled China's embodied-AI and humanoid-robot funding boom — revenue that never arrived, crowded rivals, IPO exits that closed — and who holds the losses. The inside view from mainland tech press.

stories.label: Unrest in Philippines threatens to upend US backed data centers
stories.summary: The US 'Pax Silica' tech hub planned for New Clark City — $40-70 billion of data centres — has become a target of Manila's anti-corruption protests, with Filipinos objecting to water and power demand, the local mayor saying he was never consulted, and an indigenous chieftain warning over 1,000 people could be displaced. Lead with what data centres demand of a grid that already has Asia's highest power rates, and who bears it. Keep to the documented record (Senator Imee Marcos's resolution, the mayor's and chieftain's statements); this is an advocacy outlet, so attribute its framing. Dateline Manila.

stories.label: A Japanese Spacecraft Aims to Bring Back a Bit of a Martian Moon
stories.summary: JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) launches Monday to land on Phobos and bring back samples by 2031 — the first return trip to the Mars system. Lead with the scientific question the samples answer: whether Phobos is a captured asteroid or debris blasted off Mars by an impact, which would make it carry pieces of ancient Mars. Note Japan's sample-return record from Hayabusa and Hayabusa2. Dateline Tanegashima.

stories.label: Parliament puts off vote on authorizing Sisi to send troops to Saudi Arabia until Tuesday
stories.summary: New development on the Saudi-Houthi war arc: after Egypt's defence council pledged support, Sisi has now asked parliament to authorise a combat deployment to defend Saudi Arabia, and the House, after a closed three-hour session, delayed the vote to Tuesday. Lead with the first Egyptian combat mission abroad since Yemen in 2015 being put to a vote, and the delay itself: what lawmakers hesitate over (cost, casualties, Egypt's IMF-strained economy, Saudi money). Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: Macron calls for calm in France and warns rioting must not escalate
stories.summary: Material new development since the earlier protest story: Macron addressed the nation from the Élysée after Saturday's protests turned to rioting, and the Interior Ministry now counts 2,397 people detained (up from about 1,000) and 997 officers hurt, seven seriously. Lead with the detention count more than doubling and Macron's 'those who destroyed must pay'; explain what the protests were about and why a weakened president is answering with order rather than concessions. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: 12 Killed As Truck Runs Over Devotees Near Temple In Madhya Pradesh
stories.summary: Lead with accountability: the death toll near Gwalior's Sheetla Mata temple during Navaratri has risen to 15, and Chief Minister Mohan Yadav removed the city police superintendent and suspended eight officers for negligence. The mechanism: crowd control on pilgrimage roads where heavy trucks mix with tens of thousands of devotees on foot. Dateline Gwalior.

stories.label: Media groups launch urgent bid to reopen R12m SSA spy trial to public
stories.summary: Media24, Daily Maverick, amaBhungane and the Campaign for Free Expression are challenging blanket secrecy over a R12-million State Security Agency corruption trial. The precedent: whether 'national security' can close a whole trial about spies misusing public money, or only specific evidence. Lead with who is being shielded and what the media groups want instead. Dateline Johannesburg (or Pretoria if the court sits there).

stories.label: Activists push for Pakistan to recognise and support people with albinism
stories.summary: Pakistan keeps no national count of people with albinism, so the state cannot plan schooling, sight care, skin-cancer screening or job support for them, while rising heat raises their health risk. Lead with the missing number: a population the state has never counted is a population it does not serve. Dateline the city the report centres on (likely Karachi or Lahore).

stories.label: Russia and Saudi Arabia aim to continue cooperation within OPEC+ -- Foreign Ministry
stories.summary: Russian state news agency TASS reports Lavrov and Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan reaffirmed OPEC+ cooperation, and that Bahrain's foreign minister said Gulf states value coordination with Moscow on energy markets, with Brent crude near $110 on the Iran war and Hormuz disruption. The angle: Gulf producers keep Russia close even as Washington waives and reimposes Russia oil sanctions, and the two biggest OPEC+ members stay aligned on supply while the war keeps prices high. Attribute every claim to TASS. Chart: Brent crude.

stories.label: Second Chinese Submarine Drone Mothership Emerges
stories.summary: A second, smaller Chinese vessel built to launch and recover uncrewed submarines has appeared at Guangzhou Shipyard International. The second hull means a class, not a prototype: China is building the capacity to put underwater drones at sea in numbers, which matters for undersea cables and contested straits. Lead with the shipyard and what the design reveals. Dateline Guangzhou.

stories.label: 中美AI竞争的新变量：开源、算力与产业生态
stories.summary: The view from the mainland tech press: TMTPost argues the US-China AI race is no longer about whose model is strongest, but about open weights, compute and getting models into factories, logistics and robots cheaply, with chip export controls pushing the open-versus-closed choice into state policy. Lead with the concrete claim the piece makes about open-source Chinese models' cost advantage, set against China's new AI export controls and DeepSeek's open-weight V4.1. Present it as a Chinese industry viewpoint. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: The White House's crypto chief departs: State of Crypto
stories.summary: Patrick Witt, executive director of the President's Council of Advisors for Digital Assets, is leaving for the private sector. The angle is the revolving door and the policy vacuum: who now steers US stablecoin and market-structure rules, and which firms the official who wrote them goes to work for. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Early humans in America endured climate chaos—new research
stories.summary: New research on the White Sands footprints, about 23,000 years old from the coldest part of the last ice age, finds the people who made them lived through violent swings in climate around an ancient lake. Lead with what the lake record shows about how fast conditions changed, and why it strengthens the case that humans reached the Americas thousands of years earlier than the old Clovis-first timeline. Name the journal. Dateline White Sands, New Mexico.

stories.label: Trump endorses Netanyahu in Israeli legislative elections
stories.summary: Nine days before Israel's 27 October election, the US president openly endorsed a prime minister wanted by the International Criminal Court for war crimes in Gaza, in a close race. Lead with the intervention itself and its timing; explain what Washington's backing is worth to Netanyahu's coalition math, and that the endorsement comes while Gaza's dead are still being pulled from rubble. Dateline Jerusalem.

stories.label: Mass funeral in Gaza for 75 bodies recovered from rubble
stories.summary: 75 Palestinians, most from Gaza City's Daraj neighbourhood, were buried together after their remains were recovered from homes destroyed months ago. Lead with the number and the place; the mechanism is that heavy machinery to clear rubble has been blocked from entering, so the dead stay uncounted and unburied long after the bombing. The continuation of the war's toll is the development.

stories.label: US treasury secretary tells Zelenskyy to be very careful with statements about Starlink
stories.summary: New since this morning's Starlink story: Treasury Secretary Bessent warned Zelenskyy publicly to be 'very careful' about blaming Washington for the satellite outages, Rubio confirmed Ukraine has no access to the military Starshield service, and Kyiv says US intelligence on Russian missile launches has resumed — all as Ukraine hit St Petersburg's oil terminal against Trump's demand. Lead with the leverage: a private company's network, switched on and off, as an instrument of US pressure on an ally's war. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: "Shouldn't Have Taken Place": Omar Abdullah On Attack On Srinagar-Bound Bus
stories.summary: A Srinagar-bound sleeper bus carrying Kashmiri passengers was stoned at a roadside dhaba in Haryana's Karnal district, leaving an elderly passenger bleeding. Lead with who was targeted and where — Kashmiris travelling through India's heartland — and the accountability question: whether Haryana police name and charge attackers, and Jammu and Kashmir's chief minister Omar Abdullah's demand. Place it in the pattern of attacks on Kashmiri students and traders outside the territory. Dateline Karnal.

stories.label: Captain of flydubai plane describes blocking axe blows as co-pilot attacked
stories.summary: The captain of flydubai flight FZ1073, Smit Machchhar, says his co-pilot attacked him with the cockpit's crash axe mid-flight; the plane diverted to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia. Lead with the captain's account, then the systemic question it reopens: pilot mental-health screening and the locked-cockpit rule, which since Germanwings in 2015 assumes the threat comes from the cabin. Dateline Tabuk.

stories.label: Yemen warns shareholders of Aramco oil company
stories.summary: Houthi forces told Saudi civilians to stay away from oil facilities and told investors to sell Saudi Aramco shares — a threat aimed at the world's most valuable oil producer and its listed stock, after strikes Drop Site reports hit Aramco. Lead with the warning to shareholders: the war is now targeting Saudi capital markets, not only pipelines. Name Brent crude, already near $110, and who pays. Attribute the warning to Iran's state agency Mehr; Drop Site is independent corroboration of the strikes. Dateline Sanaa.

stories.label: Trump's bid to make America cheap again has failed
stories.summary: Trump promised in 2024 to halve energy prices within a year; with the Gulf war pushing Brent crude toward $110 and US inflation rising, voters now tie higher energy bills to his administration's policies. Lead with the broken pledge measured against petrol and power prices; the mechanism is a war-driven oil shock that domestic drilling cannot offset. Name Brent crude, natural gas and US inflation. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Port in peril -- former Transnet workers recalled to cover for Durban Gateway Terminal
stories.summary: Africa's busiest container terminal is so short of skilled operators under Transnet's new private partnership that retired state workers are being recalled, while shipping lines lose patience and Transport Minister Barbara Creecy tries to reassure them. Lead with the recall; the mechanism is a privatisation deal that shed experienced labour before the new operator could run the cranes. Who pays: South African exporters and the landlocked neighbours who route through Durban. Dateline Durban.

stories.label: Iran becomes self-sufficent in gasoline production
stories.summary: President Pezeshkian says Iran no longer needs to import gasoline, a claim made under war and sanctions with Hormuz closed. Attribute it to Iran's state agency Mehr and do not state it as fact; the angle is what self-sufficiency would mean for a country that imported fuel despite holding the world's third-largest oil reserves, and the cost — consumption curbs, rationing, and refinery strain. Name Brent crude for context. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: Former commerce minister’s remarks at CCG’s forum
stories.summary: Chen Deming, China's commerce minister in 2007-2013, gives Beijing's inside view of the trade fight: why the bilateral investment treaties with the US and EU stalled, and why he rejects the Western 'overcapacity' charge against Chinese EVs and solar. Lead with his overcapacity argument and the reasoning behind it, presented as a Chinese viewpoint rather than filtered through Western framing. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog "employee-like" access
stories.summary: Anthropic has given external evaluators 'employee-like access' to assess its models' risks, and the watchdog may publish findings without the company's approval. Lead with the publication right — the precedent is independent oversight a lab cannot veto — and set it against OpenAI and Meta, which have no comparable arrangement and no legal duty to allow one. Dateline San Francisco.

stories.label: 广交会上的机器人，正在从“秀一场”走向“用一程”
stories.summary: At the 140th Canton Fair, Guangzhou robot maker Dongyi Technology runs humanoids as guides and badminton partners for three weeks, and reports that splitting work between a general LLM planner and on-device control models made a grasping task over 100 times faster than letting the LLM drive each step. Lead with that layered architecture and the 100x figure, attributed to the company; the structural point is China's push to move humanoids from expo demos to paid, continuous service. Dateline Guangzhou.

stories.label: Latvia eyes crypto tax payments in 2027 as parliament overhauls crypto taxation
stories.summary: Latvia's parliament is overhauling crypto taxation and could let residents pay personal taxes in cryptocurrency from 2027, an EU state competing to host crypto firms and tokenization under the bloc's MiCA rules. Lead with the tax-payment provision and what a state must build to accept volatile assets — conversion at receipt, who bears the price risk. Dateline Riga.

stories.label: Physicists prove a long-suspected quantum speed limit for thermalization
stories.summary: Physicists have proven a long-conjectured lower bound on how fast a quantum system can reach thermal equilibrium. Lead with what the limit is and why it matters: it caps how quickly quantum processors and quantum batteries can reset or settle, a constraint engineers have assumed but never had proven. Name the journal and the team from the paper.

stories.label: Saudi coalition helicopter crashes near Yemen
stories.summary: Two Saudi crew died when a coalition helicopter came down near Najran, the first fatalities the kingdom has reported since the latest flare-up with the Houthis, as ballistic missiles were intercepted over southwestern Saudi Arabia, Egypt weighs sending help, and Iran says it backs a 'political process'. Lead with the first Saudi deaths and the coalition's 'technical malfunction' claim, then the mechanism: a war that is widening on Saudi soil while Tehran positions itself as mediator. Dateline Najran.

stories.label: Why have France's school protests become a wider political crisis?
stories.summary: New since our clashes story: the government now says more than 1,000 people were arrested on Saturday, with over half a million marching, and looting in Paris, Marseille and Lyon. Lead with the arrest count and how school protests turned into pressure on Macron's government; note that Trump and Vance have since blamed immigration, a framing the reader should see named and weighed against what the protesters actually demand (schools, cost of living).

stories.label: Netanyahu claims anti-Israel 'smear' behind settler attack anger
stories.summary: The development since the Taybeh beating: Netanyahu's answer is to call the outrage a 'smear', while France and Belgium condemn and the EU does nothing beyond words. Lead with the gap between the attack on European diplomats and the absence of any consequence, and keep Palestinian olive farmers, attacked through the harvest season, at the centre — the diplomats were only the visible victims of a routine.

stories.label: Drone enters Lithuania from Poland, debris hits a car on rural road
stories.summary: A drone crossed into Lithuania from Poland, residents near Kaunas were told to shelter, and debris struck a car on a rural road — a NATO member's territory hit, not just overflown. Lead with the car and the shelter order; the mechanism is how drones from the Russia-Ukraine war keep spilling into NATO airspace (Romania downed two over the Black Sea a day ago) without anyone being able to stop them.

stories.label: Iran's new defence minister issues warning to the US
stories.summary: Parliament approved Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi, 68, a ballistic-missile and aerospace-industry man, as defence minister in the middle of the war with the US. Lead with what his appointment signals: Tehran is putting a weapons producer, not a field commander, in charge as it expects escalation. Mehr is Iranian state media — attribute his warning to it.

stories.label: Four sentenced to death in Lahore in 2022 blasphemy case
stories.summary: A Lahore sessions court sentenced four men to death in a blasphemy case built by the FIA's cybercrime wing from online content. Lead with the four death sentences; the mechanism is Pakistan's cyber-blasphemy prosecutions, which rights groups and families have tied to entrapment over messaging apps — the writer should say what the source says about the evidence and whether appeals are expected.

stories.label: Master: Em mensagens, Vorcaro declarou lado sem margem para dúvida: “apoiamos a direita”
stories.summary: Agência Pública's reading of jailed Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro's messages: he wrote 'we support the right', kept Flávio Bolsonaro and Nikolas Ferreira among his contacts and claimed to have helped one of them. Lead with the quote; the accountability angle is a collapsed bank's owner courting the politicians who would oversee the fallout. Written in Portuguese.

stories.label: Oil prices surge toward $110 a barrel
stories.summary: Brent crude settled at $109.86 on Friday, up 3.7%, and WTI rose with it, as the US war on Iran and the closed Strait of Hormuz squeezed supply. Name the series: Brent crude and WTI. Lead with the price and what drove it — the mine strike on a supertanker, Iran's threats to Gulf infrastructure — and who pays: oil importers such as Pakistan and Bangladesh. Mehr is Iranian state media citing Reuters; attribute accordingly.

stories.label: AI offers global economy huge risks and benefits: IMF
stories.summary: At the IMF-World Bank meetings, policymakers said spending on data centres and chips has become a key driver of global growth — and that a pullback in that investment would hit the whole economy. Lead with how much of growth now rests on AI capex; the structural point is concentration risk, with countries that build none of it still exposed to its reversal.

stories.label: 解禁1.7万亿、回购1.7万亿，美股最大的一场对赌在2027
stories.summary: A Chinese view of Wall Street: TMTPost tallies $1.7 trillion of US shares coming out of lock-up against $1.7 trillion of buybacks, setting up 2027 as a test of whether demand can absorb the supply; US households and foreign investors bought over $1 trillion of US stocks in the first half. Lead with the matched $1.7 trillion figures and explain the mechanism; keep it to the article's figures, not forecasts. Written in Chinese.

stories.label: Hacken report warns audit badges create false security as Q3 crypto losses hit $1.18B
stories.summary: Hacks cost crypto users $1.18 billion in the third quarter, and security firm Hacken says the audits projects advertise rarely cover what attackers actually hit: wallets, signing systems and third-party software. Lead with the $1.18 billion and the gap between what is audited and what is attacked — a developer reader will recognise the scope problem.

stories.label: Crypto exchanges Binance, Coinbase join West Africa scam sweep that flagged $11 million
stories.summary: Ghana and Nigeria arrested 28 people in a sweep on West African scam networks; Meta removed more than 3.7 million Facebook and Instagram accounts, pages and groups, and Binance and Coinbase helped flag $11 million. Lead with the 3.7 million accounts against 28 arrests — the platforms hosted the fraud at scale, and the mechanism is how exchanges and social networks became the scam centres' infrastructure.
